bib.title: PIQA: Reasoning about Physical Commonsense in Natural Language

question: Can language models trained on text alone answer physical commonsense questions about everyday objects and their affordances?
hypothesis: Modeling physical commonsense is a major challenge, and text-only pretrained models will lack it because of reporting bias.
contributions: PIQA, a two-choice goal/solution benchmark for physical commonsense
Adversarial cleaning of the data with AFLite
Evaluation of GPT, BERT and RoBERTa against human performance
Error analysis by edit distance and single-word pivots

method.summary: Crowdworkers on Mechanical Turk wrote a goal, a valid solution and a subtly wrong 'trick' solution, seeded by instructables.com pages. AFLite removed artifacts and produced the train/dev/test folds. GPT, BERT-Large and RoBERTa-Large were fine-tuned as two-way classifiers and compared with humans.
method.task: two-choice physical commonsense QA (goal, two solutions, pick the correct one)

datasets.name: PIQA
datasets.size: over 16,000 training QA pairs, ~2K dev, ~3K test; goals avg 7.8 words, solutions avg 21.3 words; over 3.7 million lexical tokens in training
datasets.source: crowdsourced on MTurk, seeded from instructables.com in six categories (costume, outside, craft, home, food, workshop); English only; annotator pay averaged > 15$/hr
datasets.preprocessing: AFLite: 5,000 examples used to fine-tune BERT-Large, embeddings of the rest computed, ensemble of linear classifiers on random subsets, instances highly predictable from embeddings discarded; examples with low annotator agreement removed; inputs truncated at 150 tokens (affects 1% of data)

other.extra: auxiliary language modeling loss during fine-tuning

training.objective: cross-entropy over the two options (linear layer on [CLS] hidden state per goal+solution, softmax over two); GPT adds a language modeling loss

other.stability: fine-tuning often unstable, some configurations at chance on validation, particularly BERT

inference.samples: single reported configuration per model; no seeds or runs stated
inference.prompting: each solution scored independently with goal, solution and a [CLS] token

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of questions where the correct of two solutions is chosen

eval.protocol: best grid-search config picked on validation; test reported; human accuracy by majority vote of annotators with >=90% on the qualification HIT, measured on development data

evidence.quote: Human evaluation was performed on development data

results.claim: Dataset size: over 16,000 training pairs, ~2K dev, ~3K test
results.quote: over 16,000 training QA pairs with an additional ∼2K and ∼3k held out for development and testing

limits: Only three models tested (GPT, BERT-Large, RoBERTa-Large), all 2018-2019 era; no later models.
Authors concede fine-tuning was unstable and report the best grid-search configuration on validation; hyperparameter values and seeds are not given.
Some dev 'mistakes' are correct answers needing a web search to verify.
Authors say models trained on large web crawls may eventually surpass human performance.
Human accuracy measured on dev, models reported on test.

terms.definition: a systematic data bias reduction that discards instances whose given feature representations are collectively highly indicative of the target label

lineage.note: BERT-Large also the AFLite filter model
